problem: RL agents for visual mobile manipulation (ArmPointNav in ManipulaTHOR) are evaluated only on task success and ignore collisions/disturbance of other objects; the baseline has only ~30% success without disturbance. Directly training with a disturbance penalty from scratch is unstable and collapses to early termination.
motivation: Real-world deployment requires agents that do not knock over or move irrelevant objects, but simulators impose no cost on this. Adding a penalty naively discourages exploration, so agents learn to pick up the object and immediately stop, a bad local optimum.
key_idea: Train first with the original reward to learn the task, then fine-tune with a disturbance-penalized reward (two-stage curriculum), optionally with a supervised next-step disturbance-prediction auxiliary task.
insight: The penalty from scratch causes collapse: in 16/20 trials SR is <10%, agents pick up the target in 94.1% of episodes then terminate within ~7 steps. Pre-training without penalty then fine-tuning avoids this (SRwoD 46.5 vs 10.5 from scratch, and vs 35.5 for the original-reward model) and beats PPO-Lagrangian, which is sensitive to the initial multiplier. The auxiliary task mainly improves sample efficiency at 20M frames, not asymptotic performance. A larger action space (e.g. LookDown) helps disturbance avoidance.
method: Improved baseline: modified ResNet18 depth encoder, previous-action embedding, polar goal coordinates, un-normalized advantages, GRU(512) with actor-critic heads, trained with DD-PPO; raises SR substantially over the ManipulaTHOR baseline.

Disturbance-penalized reward: r'_t = r_t + λ(d_{t-1}^objects − d_t^objects) with λ=15, d being the summed displacement of all non-target objects from their initial positions; equivalent to a soft constraint on final disturbance and allows temporary displacement.
Two-stage curriculum: stage I trains with r for 20M frames; stage II fine-tunes with r' for 25M more frames (45M total).
Disturbance-prediction auxiliary task: 2-layer MLP (hidden 128) on belief b_t predicts per-action binary disturbance c_{t+1} (threshold τ≈0.001 m) using Focal loss (γ=2, α=0.5) at weight 0.1.
Enlarged action space A_large (21 actions) adding camera and arm rotation actions, letting the agent look down and move its arm more precisely.
PPO-Lagrangian baseline: constrained-MDP formulation with a learned multiplier (λ0=1 or 15) on cumulative disturbance.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (group norm) + GRU policy trained from scratch with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: RL in ManipulaTHOR ArmPointNav (APND dataset): 19 training kitchen scenes, 45M frames, 6 seen object categories; no extra data
setting.action_space: 21 discrete low-level actions (move ahead, rotate, arm/gripper move, arm wrist rotation, camera rotation, pick up, done)
setting.privileged: ground-truth object displacements used only in training reward and aux labels; none at test time apart from the goal coordinates given by the task

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 test scenes, novel objects (360 episodes per scene set); mean over 5 seeds

numbers_note: Benchmark is ArmPointNav/ManipulaTHOR, not in the canonical list; metrics SR and SRwoD.
results: Two-stage training gives SRwoD ≈46.5–47.1% at SR ≈80–81% on novel-object test scenes, versus 35.5% SRwoD for the improved baseline trained with the original reward and 10.5% SRwoD when training from scratch with the penalty. It beats PPO-Lagrangian (15.2% SRwoD at λ0=1) by over 30 points. The improved architecture also raises baseline SR by ~11 points at 20M frames.
limitations: Evaluated only on ArmPointNav in simulation, with no real-robot experiments.
Disturbance is measured only by start/end object positions and requires tuning λ_disturb on validation; ground-truth object positions are needed for training rewards.
Even the best agent has SRwoD below 50%; the auxiliary task gives no clear asymptotic gain.
builds_on: Ye et al. auxiliary tasks (CPC|A, inverse dynamics)
compares_to: training from scratch with penalized reward
